provenance.scope: Source-audited discovery cards copied without task answers. The original read_scope belongs to the audit, not a read by a future installed agent. Candidate APIs require current installed-version and task checks.

cards.title: Two-Sample T-Test
cards.method: Independent continuous two-group mean contrast.
required_inputs: Mean contrast/common SD or unrounded standardized d
Alpha, power, direction/sidedness, allocation ratio
Independent participant count in each arm
limits: Gaussian/common-variance Student t if using these balanced routines; Welch needs matching variance inputs and method
Two-sided default must be explicit; unequal allocation is not the same problem

sources.read_scope: Complete function help, arguments, strict two-tail behavior and examples; browser read 2026-10-14. R-devel docs, not production version validation.
Relevant manual sections for t, ANOVA, proportions, chi-square and ES.w2; examples and argument conventions; not every page reviewed. Candidate basic functions, not a method allowlist.

cards.title: Linear Mixed Effects Model
cards.method: Power for the prespecified fixed contrast in its actual hierarchical Gaussian model; analytic mixed-model methods or model-matched simulation.
required_inputs: Randomization level and allocation; cluster/subject/time identifiers and all fixed/random terms.
Effect contrast and scale; residual SD versus marginal SD; all variance components/correlations.
Chosen test and finite-cluster degrees-of-freedom method; alpha, target power and design-search axis.
For simulation: seed, repetitions, failed-fit policy and Monte Carlo uncertainty.
limits: ICC plus an unspecified standardized effect does not identify all hierarchical designs.
A generic design effect or asymptotic z test does not establish finite-cluster calibration.

sources.read_scope: Official CRAN manual sections makeLmer/makeGlmer, powerSim, tests, variance modification; not an audit of all package methods.

cards.title: Power Analysis via Simulation
cards.method: Prospective mixed-model simulation matching the actual randomization, repeated measures and tested contrast.
required_inputs: Randomization unit, exact arm/site allocation, admissible participant designs and measurement times.
Outcome family/link, fixed coefficients, coding and tested contrast.
All random-effect variances/covariances and residual SD/correlation on compatible scales; the planned fitted model and test.
Seed, simulation precision, fit-failure policy and Monte Carlo interval.
limits: A standardized effect and random-effects formula alone do not define a data-generating model. Reference-time and time-averaged contrasts differ.
Inspect generated design rows after extension. A qualifying simulated grid point is not a proven exact sample-size minimum.

sources.read_scope: Official powerSim/test help and selected CRAN source sections were read; package not newly executed for this audit.
Original publication method summary was read; no claim of a complete new literature review.

cards.title: One-Way ANOVA
cards.method: Balanced fixed-effect omnibus one-way F test.
required_inputs: Number of independent groups k
Cohen f or full group means/common within-group variance with exact convention
Balanced n/group, alpha, target power
limits: Independent Gaussian common-variance observations
Omnibus equal-means null; omnibus power does not guarantee any individual post-hoc comparison

sources.read_scope: Relevant manual sections for t, ANOVA, proportions, chi-square and ES.w2; examples and argument conventions; not every page reviewed. Candidate basic functions, not a method allowlist.
Complete function help; balanced one-way group variance and per-group n convention.

cards.title: Two-Sample Proportion Test
cards.method: Two independent binomial proportions.
required_inputs: Raw p1 and p2, each in[0,1]
Allocation, alpha, target power, sidedness and one-sided direction
Chosen large-sample/exact procedure and correction
limits: Independent binary observations
Arcsine h approximation and raw-proportion normal approximation are different methods; neither is automatically an exact test

sources.read_scope: Complete function help; two-sample n, p1/p2, sidedness and strict option.
Relevant manual sections for t, ANOVA, proportions, chi-square and ES.w2; examples and argument conventions; not every page reviewed. Candidate basic functions, not a method allowlist.

cards.title: Survival Analysis (Log-Rank Test)
cards.method: Two-arm log-rank/proportional-hazards design with a documented event requirement and separately justified event-to-enrollment conversion.
required_inputs: Hazard ratio under PH, allocation ratio, sidedness, alpha and target power.
Control survival/event probability over the design horizon and a compatible treatment survival law.
Accrual distribution, whether follow-up is per-person or total study duration, censoring and any explicitly requested losses.
limits: A median requires an explicit survival-shape assumption before it defines event probabilities.
Accrual duration plus maximum follow-up alone does not define the enrollment conversion.

sources.read_scope: Official R help: usage, k allocation ratio, group event probabilities, returned sample sizes and documented approximation.

cards.title: Logistic Regression
cards.method: Power for a specified logistic coefficient or joint contrast; distinguish this from prediction-model development.
required_inputs: Target predictor type, coding/unit change and its distribution or treatment allocation.
Conditional baseline probability and specified OR; do not silently substitute marginal prevalence.
Covariate dependence relevant to information, planned test, sidedness, alpha and target power.
limits: Predictor count and outcome prevalence alone do not define coefficient power.
A cases-per-predictor rule does not substitute for test power or prediction-development criteria.

sources.read_scope: Package author documentation: single-coefficient Wald method, predictor distribution, baseline probability, covariate dependence and legacy aliases.
Official CRAN manual: development sample size is criterion based, distinct from one-coefficient testing.

cards.title: Repeated Measures ANOVA
cards.method: Within-subject omnibus time test or specified longitudinal contrast.
required_inputs: Number/timing of measurements and groups
Target omnibus time effect versus interaction/contrast
Full means+covariance or documented repeated-measures f definition
Nonsphericity epsilon or an explicit compatible covariance assumption, alpha/power, complete subject count
limits: Independent subjects; within-subject dependence specified
Do not equate a single time coefficient with the omnibus time effect
Correlation alone does not identify arbitrary covariance/nonsphericity

sources.read_scope: Function help, type, ng/nm/f and nonsphericity correction; no executed package validation.
Introductory design/simulation vignette; ANOVA_design and ANOVA_power candidate workflow; not every design or installed API tested.

cards.title: Correlation Analysis
cards.method: Power for a specified Pearson correlation test in independent paired observations; use a documented approximation or justified exact method.
required_inputs: Null and alternative correlation, sign/direction, sidedness, alpha and target power.
Independent observational pairs and distributional assumption; specify a different method for rank, partial, clustered or repeated correlations.
For precision requests: confidence level and correlation-CI method.
limits: The ordinary pwr correlation workflow is a candidate for null-zero Pearson testing, not every correlation design.
A planning correlation and anticipated CI width do not guarantee a realized interval.

sources.read_scope: Official R help for correlation-test sample size, signed alternative and null-zero method.

cards.title: Non-Inferiority / Equivalence Test
cards.method: Prespecified one-sided non-inferiority test or intersection of two one-sided equivalence tests, with margins on a defined outcome scale.
required_inputs: NI direction or both equivalence limits; expected difference/ratio, SD and raw/log scale.
Parallel versus paired/crossover design, allocation, alpha convention and target success event.
Clinical justification of margins is an external scientific input, not inferred from statistical convenience.
limits: Equivalence requires both rejection conditions; one one-sided power is not their joint power.
Defaults for bioequivalence scale/design cannot be silently applied to a parallel continuous superiority/NI problem.

sources.read_scope: Official R help: one-sided NI, raw/log scale, parallel/crossover choices and total sample-size units.
Official R help: two one-sided tests, alpha convention, exact power, margins, scale, SD and design.

cards.title: Cluster Randomized Trial
cards.method: Parallel cluster-randomized planning with a matching cluster-level or mixed-model analysis.
required_inputs: Outcome family; raw contrast and marginal SD, binary group risks, or count rates/exposure as appropriate.
Clusters per arm, allocation/stratification, cluster-size distribution, ICC and the planned test.
Alpha, direction, target power and any explicitly requested recruitment/missingness adjustments.
limits: A design effect does not create independent participants or additional cluster degrees of freedom. Fixed cluster counts can limit attainable power.
CRTSize::n4means has a valid n field for balanced allocation; inspect nE/nC for unequal allocation and check the actual interface.

sources.read_scope: Official help and selected n4means source/return fields were read; no new package execution.
Original methods overview page was read; it does not validate a particular implementation.
Official powerSim/test help and selected CRAN source sections were read; package not newly executed for this audit.

cards.title: Stepped-Wedge CRT
cards.method: Period-adjusted stepped-wedge cluster power using the actual intervention matrix and matching cohort or cross-sectional covariance.
required_inputs: Complete cluster-by-period treatment matrix, sequence counts, transitions and measurement schedule.
Outcome aggregation/family/link, baseline, raw effect and variance scale.
Cross-sectional versus cohort sampling, within-period/between-period correlations and any within-person dependence.
Period adjustment, treatment-effect timing, participant/observation units, test, alpha, power and feasible design range.
limits: Check each implementation's support for incomplete cells, unequal sizes and correlation decay; do not invent a time trend to select a code branch.

With explicit random-effect components, swCRTdesign uses residual sigma; swdpwr uses marginal sigma2. Map these and the correlation parameters from the same covariance model. Cohort observations must not be counted as distinct people.

sources.read_scope: Official help and selected CRAN source were read for covariance, scale and time-branch behavior; no new execution.
Official swPwr help/model parameterizations were read; no new numerical validation.
Original publication abstract was read for supported designs and correlation scope; full paper not claimed.

cards.title: Chi-Square Test
cards.method: Pearson contingency-table independence chi-square.
required_inputs: Rows/columns and corresponding df
Cohen w or alternative joint cell probabilities/margins
Alpha, power, total independent n
Margins/joint table if expected counts or odds ratio are requested
limits: Specified multinomial sampling and asymptotic Pearson test
Chi-square rejection uses an upper tail; omnibus association is nondirectional
w alone does not identify odds ratio or cell counts

sources.read_scope: Relevant manual sections for t, ANOVA, proportions, chi-square and ES.w2; examples and argument conventions; not every page reviewed. Candidate basic functions, not a method allowlist.

cards.title: Paired T-Test
cards.method: One-sample t test of independent pair differences.
required_inputs: Mean paired difference and SD of differences or unrounded dz
Alpha, sidedness/direction, target power
Number of complete independent pairs
limits: Normally distributed differences for exact small-sample t calibration
If SDdifference is provided, correlation is not an additional power parameter
Correlation sensitivity requires holding marginal SDs fixed and recomputing difference SD coherently

cards.title: One-Sample T-Test
cards.method: Continuous mean against a fixed known reference.
required_inputs: Fixed null mean and alternative mean
Positive observation SD, alpha, power, sidedness/direction
Independent participant count
limits: Reference value treated fixed/known, not an independently estimated sample mean
Gaussian observations for exact small-sample t calibration

sources.read_scope: Complete function help, arguments, strict two-tail behavior and examples; browser read 2026-10-14. R-devel docs, not production version validation.
Relevant manual sections for t, ANOVA, proportions, chi-square and ES.w2; examples and argument conventions; not every page reviewed. Candidate basic functions, not a method allowlist.

cards.title: One-Sample Proportion Test
cards.method: Single binomial probability against a fixed null.
required_inputs: Fixed p0 and anticipated p1
Alpha, target power, one/two-sided direction
Planned exact/approximate rejection rule and continuity convention
Independent Bernoulli count n
limits: Exact binomial rejection sets are discrete; do not label a normal/arcsine routine exact
Population reference is treated fixed; uncertainty in an estimated national rate needs another model

sources.read_scope: Function help for approximate one-proportion calculation and continuity correction. Page labels MKpower0.9; installed help must be checked.
Complete exact binomial help and alternatives; exact rejection-set power requires summing binomial probabilities, not a power function call.
Relevant manual sections for t, ANOVA, proportions, chi-square and ES.w2; examples and argument conventions; not every page reviewed. Candidate basic functions, not a method allowlist.

cards.title: McNemar's Test
cards.method: Paired binary marginal-change test.
required_inputs: Unconditional discordant joint probabilities p01 and p10 with p01+p10<=1
Alternative direction, alpha, target power
Chosen corrected/uncorrected asymptotic or conditional exact test
Number of matched pairs
limits: Discordant counts are mutually exclusive multinomial cells of the same n pairs
Do not interpret p01/p10 as probabilities conditional on being discordant unless converted
Zero discordant probability/ratio boundaries need explicit handling

sources.read_scope: Maintainer function help including paid, psi, n pairs and normal/exact/cond.exact. Documentation cell notation is inconsistent with its example: inspect installed source and check against explicit p01/p10 before mapping.
Complete function help; paired table symmetry and continuity correction.
Complete exact binomial help and alternatives; exact rejection-set power requires summing binomial probabilities, not a power function call.

cards.title: Mann-Whitney U Test (Wilcoxon Rank-Sum)
cards.method: Independent two-distribution rank-sum power.
required_inputs: Group distributions or a supported alternative/variance model
Probability superiority orientation and tie convention
Allocation, alpha, sidedness/direction and planned exact/asymptotic/corrected rank test
Seed, repetitions, failed-test treatment, Monte Carlo uncertainty for simulation
limits: A=P(X>Y)+.5P(X=Y) under ties; smaller pain may favor treatment rather than larger scores
Probability superiority alone does not universally identify alternative rank-statistic variance/power
d=sqrt(2)*qnorm(A) is conditional on equal-variance Gaussian location shift, not universal

sources.read_scope: Function help and design examples: two generators, sidedness, test options and grid. Page labels MKpower0.9; current CRAN package manual also opened; installed version must be checked.
Function help including rank-sum hypothesis, tie and exact/correction behavior. R-devel behavior can differ from deployed R.

cards.title: Multiple Linear Regression
cards.method: Documented incremental partial F test comparing nested Gaussian linear models.
required_inputs: Full/reduced models, number of tested coefficients q and full-model parameter count P excluding intercept.
Anticipated reduced/full R-squared and their compatible incremental change; allocation/design assumptions.
Alpha, target power and the chosen package-specific noncentrality convention.
limits: The corrected current template already distinguishes q, P and incremental R-squared.
pwr.f2.test mapping is not automatically a general adjusted-model mapping; verify both df and noncentrality.

sources.read_scope: Official R help: full/reduced predictor counts, f-squared and regular/Cohen convention.
Package source: exact noncentrality f2*(u+v+1) and F tails; not a general fixed-design specification.

cards.title: Two-Way ANOVA
cards.method: Power for prespecified main-effect or interaction contrasts/omnibus tests in the complete factorial Gaussian model.
required_inputs: Factor levels/cells, allocation, complete fitted model and error degrees of freedom.
Selected contrast/omnibus numerator df and effect-size definition relative to residual variance.
Which effects are requirements; separate each-test, joint and multiplicity-adjusted power.
limits: A collapsed one-way comparison and full factorial model need not have the same error df.
A scalar d does not identify an arbitrary multi-level omnibus effect.

sources.read_scope: Official R help: sample size, selected numerator degrees of freedom, f and number of groups.
Package source: exact noncentrality f2*(u+v+1) and F tails; not a general fixed-design specification.
Package source: one-way balanced numerator/residual degrees of freedom, noncentrality and per-group units.

cards.title: ANCOVA (Analysis of Covariance)
cards.method: Power for the selected adjusted group contrast/omnibus F test in a defined ANCOVA model.
required_inputs: Groups/allocation, selected contrast, number of actual covariate parameters and fitted model.
Whether f/partial eta-squared already uses adjusted residual variance, or raw means/SD plus covariate explanatory R-squared.
Covariate-outcome joint structure, treatment-covariate relationship, alpha and power.
limits: One pairwise covariate-outcome correlation does not identify multiple-covariate explanatory R-squared.
Do not apply variance reduction twice to an already adjusted effect size; gain is conditional on the model.

sources.read_scope: Package author documentation: adjusted-effect-size ANCOVA interface.
Package author documentation: means/SD, covariate explanatory variance and adjusted versus unadjusted effect conventions.

cards.title: Cox Proportional Hazards Regression
cards.method: Power for a specified Cox coefficient or contrast; identify event and covariate information separately from predictor count.
required_inputs: PH coefficient target, HR per predictor unit, predictor coding/distribution and allocation/prevalence.
Dependence of the target predictor on adjustment covariates.
Event fraction over the defined observation design or survival/accrual/censoring law; alpha, sidedness, target power.
limits: ssizeEpi.default is specifically documented for a binary target predictor and its stated covariance setup.
coxph fits data; it is not itself a power/sample-size function.

sources.read_scope: Official R help: binary target predictor, predictor prevalence, event fraction, covariate dependence and interpretation limits.
Official R help for actual Cox model fitting; fitting is not itself a power calculator.
Official CRAN manual: development sample size is criterion based, distinct from one-coefficient testing.

cards.title: Poisson Regression
cards.method: Power for a Poisson log-link coefficient with explicit predictor distribution and exposure; use a distinct method for overdispersed/clustered counts.
required_inputs: Target rate ratio per specified predictor contrast, predictor distribution/allocation and adjustment dependence.
Baseline rate and exposure units, or expected count over an explicitly defined exposure.
Conditional variance/dispersion, clustering if present, planned test, alpha and power.
limits: A predictor count alone does not determine covariate information.
Standard Poisson power does not automatically apply to negative-binomial, zero-inflated or cluster-correlated data.

sources.read_scope: Package author documentation: Poisson single-coefficient Wald procedure, exposure, predictor distribution and rate specification.

cards.title: Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE)
cards.method: Power for a prespecified marginal mean contrast with a valid joint outcome distribution and the planned GEE variance/test.
required_inputs: Outcome family/link, marginal baseline means/probabilities and marginal effect scale.
Independent subjects/clusters, allocation, measurement times and covariance/correlation structure.
Working versus data-generating dependence, missingness, variance estimator/small-cluster correction, alpha and power.
For simulation: explicit fit-failure accounting, repetitions/seed and Monte Carlo precision.
limits: A random-intercept logit variance is not an observed binary ICC, and its coefficient is not automatically a marginal OR.
A fitting package requires a matching power/simulation procedure; syntax success alone does not establish calibration.

sources.read_scope: Official CRAN manual geeglm and id/waves: within-cluster contiguous row ordering, working correlation, sandwich variance.

cards.title: Crossover Design
cards.method: Design-adjusted crossover treatment-contrast power under explicitly stated superiority, non-inferiority or equivalence hypotheses.
required_inputs: Sequences, periods, allocation, planned model, contrast and sidedness.
Marginal, residual or paired-difference SD with a compatible covariance/correlation model.
Period adjustment, carryover assumption, completeness, alpha, target power and any requested attrition.
limits: A planned washout does not prove absent carryover. An ordinary paired test can differ from the planned period-adjusted analysis.
PowerTOST::power.noninf is directional; two-sided superiority requires a verified full rejection-region calculation. Default TOST addresses a different hypothesis.
Preserve admissible sequence balance and distinguish people, sequences and measurements.

sources.read_scope: Official help and original source were read in the prior audit; directional-power scope was checked.
Original CONSORT crossover extension was read with the browser; a separate direct HTML request failed.

cards.title: Factorial Design (2×2 or Higher)
cards.method: Power for defined full-factorial contrasts or omnibus tests with the specified success and multiplicity rules.
required_inputs: Factor levels, cells, allocations, cell means or fully defined contrasts and residual variance.
Complete model, including the intended interaction terms, and selected numerator/error degrees of freedom.
Marginal versus simple effects, each-test versus joint success, alpha and multiplicity policy.
limits: A scalar standardized difference does not define an arbitrary multi-level omnibus test. Collapsing factors can change residual degrees of freedom.
A nonzero interaction can coexist with a well-defined marginal contrast. Interaction power is a separate design requirement.

sources.read_scope: Official exact-ANOVA help and noncentrality convention were read; equivalence to another target method was not established.

cards.title: Meta-Analysis Power
cards.method: Power for a pooled effect under a stated study sampling-variance and heterogeneity model, matched to the planned meta-analysis test.
required_inputs: Effect metric/scale, pooled effect, study count, within-study arm allocation and sample-size/variance distribution.
A coherent heterogeneity parameterization, estimation method and normal, t or Knapp-Hartung inference.
Alpha, target power and any modeled dependence or selection process.
limits: I-squared depends on within-study variances; it is not an independent variance scale. Heterogeneity estimation matters with few studies.

metapower::mpower uses an equal-study-size normal approximation with supplied heterogeneity. It does not reproduce every estimated-heterogeneity or Knapp-Hartung analysis. metafor fitting functions need a separate prospective power procedure.
Do not infer publication-bias effects without a specified selection model. Record simulation failures.

sources.read_scope: Official help and selected variance/power source were read; approximate equal-size method, no new execution.
Author documentation for effect estimates, variances and inference choices was read; no new model fit.
Original publication abstract was read; full article not claimed.

cards.title: Sample Size Re-estimation
cards.method: Prespecified blinded nuisance-parameter re-estimation, separated from unblinded effect-based adaptation with its own protected inference.
required_inputs: Outcome model, fixed alternative, sidedness, original design and interim timing.
What remains blinded, the nuisance estimator and whether treatment effects or conditional power enter adaptation.
Exact interim-to-final sample-size rule, admissible bounds/rounding and final test or combination rule.
Null/alternative nuisance scenarios and simulation precision when operating characteristics require evaluation.
limits: Blinding alone does not guarantee nominal Type I error for every adaptation rule. Unblinded adaptation needs a justified error-control method.
blindrecalc's documented Student interface is one-sided; do not assume automatic two-sided calibration.
Information fraction need not equal recruitment fraction; blinded pooled variance alone does not supply effect-based conditional power.

sources.read_scope: Official Student/alpha-adjustment help was read; one-sided interface, no simulation certification.
Original internal-pilot article abstract was read; full article not claimed.

cards.title: Binary Outcome Prediction Model (Riley's Method)
cards.method: Binary prediction-model development using all candidate coefficient parameters and the applicable Riley overfitting/precision criteria.
required_inputs: Outcome definition, prediction horizon and representative prevalence.
All candidate coefficient parameters, excluding intercept and counting dummy, nonlinear and interaction terms.
Conservative anticipated Cox-Snell R-squared or a documented AUC approximation with its assumptions; shrinkage/precision targets.
limits: AUC alone does not determine Cox-Snell R-squared. An approximation requires prevalence and score-distribution assumptions.
Planning criteria do not guarantee realized shrinkage, prediction error or event counts. Report each requirement and the governing maximum.

sources.read_scope: Official help and selected binary/survival/continuous/AUC-conversion source were read; no new production test.
Original Part II sections and abstract were read; correction identified with limited full-text access. Current implementation still needs checking.

cards.title: Survival Outcome Prediction Model (Riley's Method)
cards.method: Time-to-event prediction-model development with horizon-risk precision and conditional overfitting criteria.
required_inputs: Event, censoring and competing-risk definitions and prediction horizon.
Event rate with time units, compatible mean follow-up and anticipated Cox-Snell R-squared.
All candidate coefficient parameters, shrinkage and any additional follow-up/accrual assumptions.
limits: An event probability is not a hazard/rate. Inspect the package's working survival and risk assumptions.
A fully observed fixed-horizon binary target may be a binary model; recurrence terminology alone does not force a Cox model.
Do not invent an effective event-rate correction for competing risks. Use a matching source-supported method.

sources.read_scope: Official help and selected binary/survival/continuous/AUC-conversion source were read; no new production test.
Original Part II sections and abstract were read; correction identified with limited full-text access. Current implementation still needs checking.

cards.title: Continuous Outcome Prediction Model (Riley's Method)
cards.method: Continuous prediction-model development using the four relevant overfitting and precision requirements.
required_inputs: Outcome units, target-population mean and marginal SD.
All candidate coefficient parameters and conservative anticipated adjusted R-squared.
Shrinkage and precision requirements, including the meaning of the mean/intercept precision criterion.
limits: Inspect residual SD precision rather than relabeling it residual variance precision. Defaults are not universal thresholds.
Increasing anticipated R-squared can change a particular requirement while the governing maximum remains set by another criterion.
Check applicability for near-zero outcome means and the specified residual distribution.

sources.read_scope: Official help and selected binary/survival/continuous/AUC-conversion source were read; no new production test.
Original Part I abstract and criteria were read; not a new verification of every formula.

cards.title: Prediction Model External Validation Sample Size
cards.method: External validation of a fixed prediction model using metric-specific precision in the intended population.
required_inputs: Fixed model, external population, outcome/horizon and censoring definition.
Anticipated outcome frequency, discrimination, calibration and the linear-predictor distribution as required by the method.
Explicit CI-width/precision requirements for each metric; decision threshold and net-benefit precision if requested.
limits: The audited pmvalsampsize interface supports binary outcomes; do not apply it unchanged to survival concordance or continuous R-squared.
Event-count rules do not guarantee calibration or decision-curve precision. Validation can require more participants than development.
Model updating/refitting is a different estimation task and needs its own design.

sources.read_scope: Official binary-validation help/source were read; no new package execution.
Original validation-method criteria and worked example were read; no universal event-count guarantee inferred.

cards.title: High-Dimensional Prediction Model (Machine Learning / Penalized Regression)
cards.method: Prospective simulation or learning-curve planning of the complete high-dimensional prediction pipeline.
required_inputs: Outcome/horizon/censoring, feature distributions/correlation, sparsity, effect/noise assumptions or another justified data generator.
Preprocessing, selection, tuning and validation design, including leakage prevention.
Explicit prediction/calibration/stability goals, outcome frequency or variance, and assurance/simulation precision.
limits: glmnet functions fit and tune models; they are not sample-size calculators. Alpha/lambda tuning and outer evaluation must be specified.
Applying regression planning only to the selected predictor count does not account for selection/search cost.
No universal events-per-feature multiplier guarantees stability across penalized and machine-learning methods. Selection frequency is not selection power.

sources.read_scope: Official fitting/tuning help and selected source were read; not a sample-size-function validation.
